title: The same request bytes are parsed twice — once as HTTP, once as a command line — so a CLI-only option parser becomes remotely settable
index_line: T-0022 · CODE_EXEC · argv populated from the query string reaches a CLI option reader with no SAPI check · php/cgi-inherited · corroborated
invariant_violated: Code written to be reached only from the command line assumes that `argv` is the process's command line. With `register_argc_argv` on — the PHP default, and the default in the official Craft image — PHP fills `$_SERVER['argv']` from the query string, split on spaces. Every CLI-only option parser in the process is then remotely settable, and none of them checked `PHP_SAPI`.

mechanism.does: the attacker sends a query string whose space-separated tokens look like command-line options (`?--templatesPath=…`)
the runtime populates the request's argv from the query string because `register_argc_argv` is on, indistinguishable from a real CLI invocation
the application bootstrap resolves its paths and settings through a CLI option reader that reads argv with no SAPI guard
the attacker's option wins over the configured default, so a path that decides what code is loaded is now attacker-chosen
wrapper choice matters: http:// and php:// fail an existence check (no stat support), but ftp:// supports stat
the remote resource is fetched and rendered as a template, so the attacker's template source executes in the engine
the engine's sandbox denylists dangerous function *names* passed as filter arguments

source.http.request.value: the query string — the second parse of the same bytes; the payload is `?--option=value` and nothing else

sink.eval.value: the template render (or any CLI-configurable path that decides what gets loaded/evaluated)

guard.none.value: the missing `PHP_SAPI === 'cli'` check in the option reader; the existence check that was supposed to guard the path instead selects the wrapper

encoding.shell.value: argv token shape: `--flag`, `--flag=value`, `+token` — spaces (or `+`) are the argument separator, so a value containing a space splits

gadget.engine-escape.value: the indirect-invocation bypass of a name denylist: `sort('call_user_func')` calls a permitted name that then calls the forbidden one

preconditions.expr: register_argc_argv is on (PHP default; on in the official Craft Docker image; off on many shared hosts)
the application has a CLI option reader that is reachable during a web bootstrap (shared bootstrap for console and web)
a settable option decides a path that is included, required or read-and-evaluated (templates, config, migrations, storage)
no PHP_SAPI guard anywhere on the option-reading path

success: `?--templatesPath=<remote>` changes what the app loads — a template rendered from an attacker-controlled source returns attacker output
a bogus option (`?--configPath=/nonexistent`) provably breaks the app, proving argv is attacker-writable before any exploit is attempted
the same request is inert when register_argc_argv is off — the differential is the proof
failure_like: register_argc_argv is off — `$_SERVER['argv']` is absent and `?--flag` is inert
the option reader is only instantiated on a genuine CLI entry point (a separate binary that the web bootstrap never loads)
the existence check rejects every stream wrapper (or the engine refuses remote template sources)
false_positive: a `?--flag` request that 404s or 500s because the option simply does not exist — that shows argv is reachable, not that a dangerous option is
`--help`-style output reflected into the page without changing what is loaded
treating the resulting SSTI as the discovery when the argv reachability is the finding — they are two bugs and the report should say both

hazards: this is a runtime footgun, so it recurs in any PHP application that shares one bootstrap between CLI and web — hunt for `argv` readers, not for Craft
the separator is a space (or `+`), so a value containing a space needs encoding; that constraint shapes every payload
the wrapper selection is the clever part: an existence check is not a security control, and `ftp://` supporting stat turns it into a selector
non_transfers: languages without the argv-from-query-string behaviour (Python/Node/Ruby WSGI servers do not populate a CLI argument vector from the query string)
PHP deployments with register_argc_argv=Off (many shared hosts and several distros) — the whole class dies there
CLI option readers guarded by PHP_SAPI
